title: Build a Blog Aggregator in Go
description: Build a database-backed Go CLI that collects and manages RSS feeds.

lessons.title: Welcome to the Blog Aggregator
lessons.instruction: This project is a CLI pipeline: load configuration, fetch an RSS feed, parse its items, then store new posts. Put the missing parse stage between fetching and storage.

lessons.title: Config
lessons.instruction: The CLI keeps the active username in a small JSON config file. Update the typed config before it is encoded back to disk; the JSON tag keeps the file format stable.

lessons.title: Commands
lessons.instruction: A command registry maps a command name to a handler. Register the login handler so dispatch can validate its argument and run it without a switch statement.

lessons.title: Postgres
lessons.instruction: The aggregator stores feeds and posts in PostgreSQL. Run Check to verify that the course database accepts a live connection.
lessons.expected: PASS · The live postgres services are ready.

lessons.title: Goose Migrations
lessons.instruction: Goose records applied migration versions and runs the remaining versions in order. Build the pending list without reapplying version 1.

lessons.title: SQLC
lessons.instruction: SQLC generates typed parameter and row types from SQL. Application code should build those parameters rather than editing generated query code; pass the requested name into the generated-style parameter value.

lessons.title: Reset
lessons.instruction: Reset is intentionally destructive. Without cascading deletes, child rows must be removed before the feeds and users they reference; put the tables in foreign-key-safe order.

lessons.title: List Users
lessons.instruction: List every persisted user and mark the one selected in configuration. Set the marker only when the row matches the current username.

lessons.title: RSS
lessons.instruction: RSS is XML: channel metadata and repeated item elements map cleanly to tagged Go fields. Correct the XML tags so the feed title and both items are decoded.

lessons.title: Feeds
lessons.instruction: A feed has a canonical URL and an owner, and the database should keep the URL unique. Prevent a second record from being added for an existing URL.

lessons.title: List Feeds
lessons.instruction: A joined feed query can return display-ready rows containing the feed name, URL, and owner's username. Include all three values in each rendered row.
lessons.expected:
Go Blog | https://go.dev/blog | alice
Go Time | https://changelog.com/gotime/feed | bob

lessons.title: Follow
lessons.instruction: Following is a many-to-many relationship. Treat the user/feed pair as unique so repeating the same follow command is idempotent while another user may still follow that feed.

lessons.title: Middleware
lessons.instruction: Authenticated command middleware resolves the configured user once, rejects a missing login, and passes a typed user to the real handler. Inject the selected user instead of an empty value.

lessons.title: Unfollow
lessons.instruction: Unfollow removes only the current user's relationship to one feed. Filter by both IDs so another user's follow and the current user's other feeds remain intact.

lessons.title: Aggregate
lessons.instruction: A fair aggregator selects an unfetched feed first, then the feed fetched least recently. Fix the scheduler so a new feed is not starved by a recently fetched one.

lessons.title: Posts
lessons.instruction: Feed polling sees the same items repeatedly. Keep a stable item URL or GUID unique so an existing post is skipped instead of inserted again.

lessons.title: Docs
lessons.instruction: The README should cover installation, database setup, migrations, configuration, and every command. Add the aggregation command and its duration argument to the concise command reference.

lessons.title: Submit Your Repo!
lessons.instruction: A ready repository is formatted, tested, documented, and includes migrations and generated query code without committing credentials. Mark the test check complete so the final audit passes.
